exploitation_conditions.statement: An attacker would need to invoke Docker's network creation APIs (e.g., via Docker API with NetworkCreate requests) on a Docker daemon using a version between 26.0.0 and 26.0.2 on a host with IPv4-only network interfaces. Trivy does not expose Docker API network endpoints, does not create Docker networks, and does not call any network-related Docker client APIs. There is no attack-reachable path from Trivy's attack surfaces (image scanning via CLI, OCI artifact processing, registry operations) to the vulnerable code.

vulnerability_mechanism.summary: CVE-2024-32473 allows IPv6 to be enabled on IPv4-only network interfaces in the Docker daemon. This is a network configuration defect where Docker creates network interfaces with IPv6 support even when the underlying host interface is IPv4-only, potentially causing unintended network exposure or misconfiguration. The effect occurs because the affected docker/docker code path handles network creation/management in the Docker daemon, not in the client library.

root_cause.summary: The advisory GO-2024-2737 binds to module github.com/docker/docker, introduced in 26.0.0+incompatible and fixed in 26.0.2+incompatible. The vulnerable code resides in the Docker daemon's network layer within the docker/docker module. In this Trivy snapshot, docker/docker is imported as a dependency at go.mod:45 (v26.0.1+incompatible). The code in Trivy that uses docker/docker (pkg/fanal/image/daemon/docker.go:7-9 imports github.com/docker/docker/client) only calls read-only image APIs (ImageInspectWithRaw, ImageHistory, ImageSave). No network creation or management APIs are invoked.

alternative_paths.summary: Checked: (1) All docker/docker imports in the snapshot - confirmed only client and types APIs used, no daemon/network code. (2) All docker docker client method calls - only ImageInspectWithRaw, ImageHistory, ImageSave, ImageLoad, ImageTag, ImageRemove. (3) Integration tests (integration/docker_engine_test.go) only test image loading, inspection, and removal. (4) Containerd and podman daemon readers (containerd.go, podman.go) do not use docker network APIs. (5) Searched for any network creation API calls - zero matches. Not fully explored: transitive dependencies within docker/docker that may have different usage patterns not visible from import analysis alone (the docker/docker client package may internally reference network-related types even if only image APIs are called). However, Go packages are typically not linked if their symbols are not referenced, and the CVE affects daemon-side network logic, not client-side code.

Trivy uses the docker/docker client only for read-only image operations: ImageInspectWithRaw (docker.go:40,43), ImageHistory (docker.go:49), ImageSave (docker.go:66 via imageOpener), and ImageLoad/ImageTag/ImageRemove in tests (docker_engine_test.go:240,246,254). A full search for ContainerCreate, NetworkCreate, NetworkConnect, NetworkDisconnect, VolumeCreate, or any network/container/volume creation APIs found no matches in the entire snapshot. The vulnerable code path in docker/docker requires invocation of Docker network management APIs, which Trivy never calls. Therefore, the vulnerable surface has no execution path from any attack surface in Trivy's analyzed scope.
